A single-subject craft DOCUMENTATION photograph: the Front Buttonholes is the dominant subject, filling 40–80% of the frame and identifiable within one second.

A premium bespoke sport coat featuring a precise By Machine (Front Buttonholes).

Distinguishing construction detail (reproduce exactly as drawn): Machine-stitched buttonholes — precise.

Exact specification — buttonhole method: machine-sewn; eyelet holes — matching the illustration precisely.

MANDATORY GEOMETRY COVERAGE — reproduce from the illustration, exactly and without assumption, every one of these: front buttonhole construction (hand vs machine), stitch density and keyhole, thread. Match each to the drawing.

VIEW — this illustration is the front of the garment. Photograph the same face; never substitute a different face of the garment.

BLUEPRINT LOCK — THE DRAWING IS LAW: the attached technical illustration is the manufacturing blueprint for this exact craft option and the SOLE authority for the image. Reproduce its geometry precisely — edge and point shape, lengths, widths, depths, angles, curvature, roll lines, symmetry, button/buttonhole/tab positions, seam and stitch placement, proportions. Assume NOTHING from tailoring convention or model priors. Do not redesign, reinterpret, substitute a similar commercial style, stylise or "improve" it, and never fall back to a generic version of the category — render THIS option, not a typical one. If convention conflicts with the drawing, the drawing wins. ANNOTATIONS ARE NOT THE GARMENT: any numbers, units, dimension or leader lines, arrows, callouts, ruler ticks, text labels or red/coloured guide marks on the drawing are manufacturing documentation, not features of the cloth — render none of them. COLOUR IN THE DRAWING IS NOTATION: a red or tinted region marks WHERE the option sits and flat grey marks the EXTENT of a panel; render those areas in the cloth and thread of the garment itself, with no red, no highlighter tint and no flat grey panel.

Photographed worn on a male model.

Frame macro on the front buttonhole; the detail must read clearly and sharply.

Savile Row and high-end Italian sartorial aesthetic. Natural daylight studio lighting, medium-format camera, magazine-quality editorial menswear photography, authentic bespoke craftsmanship and fine hand stitching. SET — clean luxury studio, seamless plain neutral light-grey background, clear separation between garment and background: no location, architecture, furniture, scenery or props.

Extremely realistic textured wool/hopsack with visible weave texture, fine stitching.

Avoid: generic menswear substitution in place of the drawn option; illustration or line-art style; CGI or 3D-render look; cartoon; mannequin; fashion sketch; inaccurate geometry; altered proportions; missing construction details; watermark; AI-art appearance; a bare chest or missing shirt; and any text or annotation traced from the drawing — no measurement numbers, units, dimension or leader lines, arrows, callouts, ruler ticks, labels or coloured guide marks anywhere in the frame. Real garment photography of the exact drawn option — clean cloth only.

FORBIDDEN FOR THIS OPTION — do not render: a generic version of this part standing in for the exact drawn option (generic-category substitution); any feature, count, or geometry borrowed from a neighboring craft option on the same field; a feature that belongs on the opposite face of the garment from what this illustration shows (front/back/side confusion).
checklist: buttonhole method reads as machine-sewn
present & positioned as drawn: eyelet holes
distinguishing detail present: Machine-stitched buttonholes — precise.
reproduced from the illustration: front buttonhole construction (hand vs machine)
reproduced from the illustration: stitch density and keyhole
reproduced from the illustration: thread
orientation matches the illustration: front
the Front Buttonholes dominates the frame (40–80%), identifiable within one second, framed macro on the front buttonhole
silhouette, proportions, seam & stitch placement match the illustration; left/right symmetry correct
NO generic-category substitution — this exact option, not a typical one
a real photograph of the exact drawn option — not the line-art, no stylisation
